fault_line: Is CENTCOM defending America -- or dragging it back into a war the voters just rejected? Blockade as deterrence vs blockade as provocation.

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- Kent said it] Joe Kent, former head of the US National Counterterrorism Center who resigned over the US-Israel war on Iran, posted on X that CENTCOM's decision to extend its blockade to Iran's land borders is a 'brash provocation': 'This is CENTCOM inviting Iran to escalate while the Vice President is attempting to negotiate with the Iranians.' He called it 'policy by CONOP' -- 'when the military finds a way to subvert the White House without blatantly disobeying the President, by taking actions that will ensure a war escalates or perpetuates.' He warned Iran would not accept being throttled, that 'enforcing the blockade keeps our troops in harm's way and risks a shoot-down that would inevitably launch us back into kinetic war', and that voters chose an end to the war in Tuesday's midterms; CENTCOM 'must support that'. He added the President 'needs to install a new national security team, one that's not tied to starting the war and that can instead end it.' [CONTEXT -- the task force itself, already recorded 1900-01] CENTCOM announced Task Force Iron Gate on Nov 7: ~20 civilian+military staff based in Tampa, Florida, coordinating with US agencies to disrupt movement of advanced weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM claims the naval blockade has blocked more than $25bn of Iranian crude exports (CENTCOM's own figure, unverified). [SCOPE -- not a deployment] Dawn/Reuters/Geopolitiki: the task force is an internal coordination cell, not a deployed force; the statement gives no operating locations, authorities, or agreements with neighbouring states. CENTCOM's graphic names Iran's borders with Turkiye, Afghanistan, Turkmenistan and Pakistan (900km Pakistan border per Dawn).
sections.what_verified: Kent's words carried by Al Jazeera (T2) quoting his X posts; the underlying Iron Gate announcement corroborated by CENTCOM primary (T1 STATE US) + Reuters (T1) + Al Jazeera (T2) + Dawn (T3) + Times of India (T3) + Haaretz (T3). Kent's accusation of CENTCOM's intent is his own allegation -- no second source confirms the motive; recorded as his claim, not as fact about CENTCOM.
sections.what_disputed: No White House, Pentagon or CENTCOM response to Kent's accusation as of last check. CENTCOM frames Iron Gate as interagency coordination reinforcing a successful blockade, not escalation. Kent resigned over the war, so his framing is that of a dissenting former official, not a neutral assessment. The $25bn crude-blocked figure is CENTCOM's own and unverified.
sections.why_matters: The split inside Washington: Trump's own former counterterrorism chief says the generals are subverting the Vice President's negotiations -- the land blockade is the proof. Proven topic (Iran/Gulf + shipping war), hard numbers ($25bn, 20-person Tampa cell, 900km Pakistan border).
